output.summary: KEP-961 proposes adding a `maxUnavailable` field to the StatefulSet `.spec.updateStrategy.rollingUpdate` settings so that RollingUpdate can replace multiple Pods at a time instead of one. It accepts an absolute positive number or a percentage of desired pods, defaulting to 1. The KEP is currently at status implementable, stage beta.
output.rationale: StatefulSet RollingUpdate replaces Pods one at a time, which makes rollouts slow for applications with slow startup or many tolerant followers. The proposal lets users opt in to bringing down up to maxUnavailable Pods concurrently. The default of 1 keeps the previous behavior for everyone else, and the drawback of higher unavailability is accepted as a user choice.

alternatives.option: Keep StatefulSets rolling one Pod at a time and use Deployments for faster rollouts
alternatives.why_not: The readme says users who need faster rollouts with stable identity would otherwise have to give up StatefulSets, or accept Deployment workarounds for the metrics and revision-tracking scenarios.

alternatives.option: Use OnDelete update strategy and write a custom controller to delete multiple Pods in a chosen order
alternatives.why_not: The readme lists this as an alternative that gives ultimate flexibility but requires more work from the user.

evidence.quote: This new field can be an absolute, positive number (eg. `5`) or a percentage of desired pods (ex: `10%`).
When the field is not specified, it will default to 1 to maintain previous behavior of rolling one pod at a time.
If StatefulSet supported maxUnavailable with value greater than 1, it would allow for a faster rollout since a total of maxUnavailable number of pods could be loading up the cache at the same time.
It can lead to increased application unavailability/outage during rollouts when this feature is enabled and used (maxUnavailable set to values greater than 1).
